title: Ukrainian troops are buying war robots from their digital marketplace in record numbers
excerpt: Ground robots are among the "fastest-growing categories" for Ukraine's state-backed innovation platform Brave1, an official said.
content_html:
By Jake Epstein

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Ukrainian troops are rushing to a digital weapons marketplace to buy record numbers of ground robots, reflecting the surging popularity of these combat machines on the battlefield.

Brave1, the Ukrainian state-backed innovation platform, said on Monday that the military has ordered more than 3,000 ground robots from its digital marketplace since it launched last year, including over 640 units in July alone.

That latter figure represents a 680% increase over 2025's monthly average, Brave1 said in a statement.

Yuliia Myrna, product manager for the Brave1 Market digital site, said in remarks shared with Business Insider that ground robots and interceptor drones "are among the fastest-growing categories we are seeing in 2026."

Ukraine launched the Brave1 Market in April 2025, granting soldiers access to an Amazon-style website to buy military technology, such as drones, robots, and electronic warfare systems, from the defense industry, streamlining the procurement process.

In October 2025, uncrewed ground vehicles became eligible for purchase with "ePoints," which Ukrainian troops collect for verified kills of Russian soldiers or military hardware, and the completion of other battlefield tasks.

Various drone types, including first-person-view (FPV) quadcopters, interceptors, and heavy bombers, are among the most popular items on the Brave1 Market by quantity.

While ground robots can cost tens of thousands of dollars — typically making them far more expensive than these other drones — they serve in drastically different roles and have a longer operational lifecycle.

Myrna said Ukraine is "deliberately accelerating" the integration of ground robots into combat operations, particularly for logistics and casualty evacuation.

"Military units now earn ePoints for successfully completing these missions with robotic systems, creating an incentive to replace personnel in high-risk tasks wherever possible," she said.

"This creates a powerful development cycle," Myrna added, explaining that "more battlefield use generates more operational feedback for manufacturers, which leads to faster product improvements and ultimately helps us move people away from missions that can be performed by machines."

Only a few Ukrainian companies produced ground robots at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion. Today, there are roughly 280 firms that make hundreds of different products, Andrii Hrytseniuk, Brave1's CEO, told Business Insider.

The growing popularity of uncrewed ground vehicles on the Brave1 Market reflects Ukraine's broader push to replace soldiers with robots and drones in dangerous missions, particularly front-line supply runs.

Ukrainian officials have said they want robots to handle 100% of battlefield logistics, missions that have become particularly deadly as the "kill zone" — the drone-saturated area that surrounds the front line — continues to expand.

Ukrainian commanders told Business Insider that the robots allow their units to perform critical tasks while keeping troops out of harm's way.

Grek, a UGV company commander with the 21st Unmanned Systems "Kraken" Regiment, who asked to only be identified by his call sign, said that "the stakes of removing humans from dangerous missions are significant."

"Every time a person is exposed to a high-risk environment, there is a possibility of injury, loss of life, or reduced combat effectiveness," he said. "Protecting personnel means preserving experience, training, and leadership that cannot easily be replaced."

作者：Jake Epstein 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

乌克兰军队正涌向数字武器市场，购买创纪录数量的地面机器人，这反映出这些作战机器在战场上的受欢迎程度激增。

乌克兰国家支持的创新平台 Brave1 周一表示，自去年推出以来，军方已从其数字市场订购了 3,000 多台地面机器人，其中仅 7 月份就订购了 640 多台。

Brave1 在一份声明中表示，后一个数字比 2025 年的月平均值增长了 680%。

Brave1 Market 数字网站产品经理 Yuliia Myrna 在接受 Business Insider 采访时表示，地面机器人和拦截无人机“是我们在 2026 年看到的增长最快的类别之一”。

乌克兰于 2025 年 4 月推出了 Brave1 市场，允许士兵访问亚马逊风格的网站，从国防工业购买无人机、机器人和电子战系统等军事技术，从而简化了采购流程。

2025 年 10 月，无人驾驶地面车辆有资格通过“ePoints”购买，乌克兰军队通过核实击杀俄罗斯士兵或军事装备以及完成其他战场任务而收集这些车辆。

从数量来看，各种无人机类型，包括第一人称视角 (FPV) 四轴飞行器、拦截机和重型轰炸机，都是 Brave1 市场上最受欢迎的商品。

虽然地面机器人可能花费数万美元——通常比其他无人机贵得多——但它们的作用截然不同，并且具有更长的运行生命周期。

米尔纳表示，乌克兰正在“刻意加速”地面机器人融入作战行动，特别是后勤和伤员疏散方面。

她说：“军事单位现在可以通过机器人系统成功完成这些任务来获得 ePoints，从而激励他们尽可能地替换执行高风险任务的人员。”

“这创造了一个强大的开发周期，”米尔纳补充道，并解释说，“更多的战场使用为制造商带来了更多的操作反馈，从而加快了产品改进速度，并最终帮助我们让人们远离可以由机器执行的任务。”

在俄罗斯全面入侵之初，只有少数乌克兰公司生产地面机器人。 Brave1 首席执行官 Andrii Hrytseniuk 告诉 Business Insider，如今，大约有 280 家公司生产数百种不同的产品。

无人驾驶地面车辆在 Brave1 市场上越来越受欢迎，反映出乌克兰更广泛地推动用机器人和无人机取代士兵执行危险任务，特别是前线补给任务。

乌克兰官员表示，他们希望机器人能够处理 100% 的战场后勤任务，随着“杀伤区”（前线周围无人机饱和的区域）不断扩大，这些任务变得尤其致命。

乌克兰指挥官告诉《商业内幕》，这些机器人可以让他们的部队执行关键任务，同时保证部队免受伤害。

格雷克是第 21 无人系统“海妖”团的 UGV 连指挥官，他要求只透露自己的呼号，他表示“将人类从危险任务中撤离的风险非常大。”

“每当一个人暴露在高风险环境中时，就有可能受伤、丧生或战斗力下降，”他说。 “保护人员意味着保留不易被取代的经验、培训和领导力。”
